chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Maythamī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
I heard him saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disciplined His Messenger until He made him upright upon what He willed, then He delegated to him.
So He, Mighty is His remembrance, said: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”
So whatever Allah delegated to His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), He has indeed delegated it to us.

key_terms.أَدَّبَ: disciplined and refined through divine تربيت until perfection
key_terms.إِلَيْنَا: to us, referring to the Imams (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.الرَّسُولُ: the Messenger whose command is to be obeyed
key_terms.رَسُولَهُ: His Messenger, Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم)
key_terms.عَزَّ ذِكْرُهُ: exalted is His mention; a reverential expression for Allah
key_terms.فَانْتَهُوا: refrain and desist from what is forbidden
key_terms.فَخُذُوهُ: take it and accept it in obedience

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Allah’s delegation of authority to the Messenger and the Imams (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, perfected the tarbiyah of His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) and then entrusted him with delegated authority in the religion. By citing the Qur'anic command to take what the Messenger gives and refrain from what he forbids, the narration presents the authority of the Messenger and, in continuation, the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) as divinely grounded.
